extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: curating passages from Wikipedia, crowdsourcing question-answers on those passages, and obtaining additional answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: If a question was not answerable by a span in the paragraph, workers were asked to submit the question without marking an answer. Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia obtained using Project Nayuki's Wikipedia's internal PageRanks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual paragraphs were extracted from articles, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of a paragraph. Questions were entered in a text field, and answers were highlighted in the paragraph. Workers were encouraged to ask questions in their own words without copying phrases, reinforced by a reminder prompt and disabling copy-paste functionality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform, with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: At least 2 additional answers were obtained for each question in the development and test sets to evaluate human performance and make evaluation more robust. Disagreement analysis showed that mismatch occurs mostly due to inclusion/exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental disagreements about the answer.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 answer per question in the training set; at least 3 answers (1 original + at least 2 additional) per question in the development and test sets.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Located in the United States or Canada
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions with span-based answers are more constrained than the more interpretative questions found in more advanced standardized tests.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Reading Comprehension (RC) task. The dataset is partitioned into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).
